root.name: Italian Game: Deutz Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. O-O Nf6 5. d4

overview: After 4.O-O Nf6 White plays 5.d4 in the style of the Møller Attack, striking the centre at once. In the main line 5...exd4 6.e5 d5 7.exf6 dxc4 8.Re1+ Be6 9.Ng5 Qd5 the play is forcing and both kings are exposed. White fights for the initiative with lead in development against Black's extra material.

white_ideas.idea: Break the centre with d4 and open lines against the black king
Regain material with e5 and use the lead in development
Use Re1 and Ng5 to create threats against the king and f7

black_ideas.idea: Accept the pawn and return material to defend with ...d5
Neutralise the attack with accurate defensive moves and trade queens
Counterattack the bishop on c4 and the e-pawn

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after d4 exd4 with White pieces aimed at the kingside

character.notes: Forcing, tactical lines with open kings and early piece activity.

gambit.notes: After 5...exd4 6.e5 d5 White's compensation relies on lead in development; Black can choose to return material.

soundness.notes: Probably sound; viable if not objectively better for White.

approach.notes: A rare gambit in the Italian that strong players seldom choose.

level.notes: Needs concrete theory but is rare, so Intermediate.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5...Bxd4
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. O-O Nf6 5. d4 Bxd4 6. Nxd4 Nxd4
sublines_that_differ.how: Black trades the bishop for the d4 pawn and knight for a quieter game.

character.reason: Early d4 break leads to forcing, open play.

gambit.reason: White offers material for development and attack.

soundness.reason: Compensation is reasonable but unproven, like other Italian gambits.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose this branch.

plans.reason: Development lead and Ng5 ideas against f7.
